PullRequest.Title: Show Dev Container startup progress in the chat view
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #335661.

- Switch to the chat-in-progress view while the Dev Container Agent Host is being prepared, instead of leaving the new-session composer visible.
- Stream startup phases and a bounded Dev Container CLI output tail into an expandable Output section with cancellation and keyboard/screen reader support.
- Preserve the prompt and attachments when preparation fails or is cancelled, and surface setup errors through notifications.
- Add regression coverage and update the Sessions architecture documentation and accessibility help.

## Validation

- Targeted unit suites: 613 passing, 13 pending.
- Client typecheck, changed-file ESLint, CSS stylelint, layering checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Dev Container smoke tests against the current source build, with tracing enabled: **2 passing, none skipped**:
  - Starts a session in a Dev Container.
  - Starts and reopens a Dev Container session over WSL.
- Live smoke environment: Windows, Docker Desktop 4.91.0 with WSL integration, WSL 2.7.14, and Ubuntu 24.04.

Scenarios.Scenario: Submit, cancel, and retry the first request for a Dev Container draft in the Agents window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The foreground send waits for provider preparation: optional availability resolution, workspace trust/config resolution, optional eager draft creation and detached-worktree setup, Dev Container connection/Agent Host discovery, replacement-session configuration, then chat creation and request send. Progress rendering runs alongside those awaited steps and does not add another boundary operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Dev Container availability and connect through the shared-process or source remote-host service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One availability operation per draft preference and one logical connect per workspace; the service coalesces cold concurrent connects in _pendingConnections and reuses _activeConnections.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same availability and connect operations were already awaited; the diff exposes phase state and cancellation around them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Availability and connect must complete before the first request can be sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the Dev Container CLI for a cold container connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One CLI process for the cold logical connection, with reconnects managed by the existing connection transport; no per-progress-message spawn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The CLI was spawned with the same argument list and environment clone; the diff only removes debugger variables from that clone.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold Dev Container startup blocks the first request as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optionally create, claim, or roll back one detached worktree through the source Agent Host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one detached worktree per worktree-isolated draft; cancellation before creation prevents this boundary, and failure/cancellation after creation rolls it back.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The worktree operations were already performed; the diff makes the eager-create wait cancellable and adds bounded phase updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: For worktree isolation, creation and claim remain on the first-request critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the replacement chat and send the initial request after preparation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create-chat and one send per successful draft submission; canceled preparation does not reach them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider calls occurred after preparation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations complete the user-visible send after container preparation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active draft and one selected workspace, with an optional single detached worktree. Progress cardinality is phase-count, not CLI-output-line count; tests cover multiple phase updates retaining one temporary chat view.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Preparation uses one token per submitted draft. Cold connections are coalesced per normalized workspace by _pendingConnections; retries reuse availability state and active connections where valid. The optional worktree operations remain serial. Progress has only a constant number of phase transitions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Availability is retained per draft, output channels are keyed by normalized workspace hash, pending connections coalesce cold callers, and active connections are reused. Cancellation clears transient progress and temporary UI while existing provider cleanup rolls back worktrees/connections.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed UI state and all transitive preparation boundaries were traced, and tests explicitly show one preparation view across multiple progress values plus disposal on cancellation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual container and remote-host startup duration varies widely, but the diff does not add or multiply those boundary calls. The extra temporary chat view is held only for the bounded preparation lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change adds one visible chat view and constant phase rendering while preserving boundary cardinality and cleanup; the extra work is bounded and required for the progress surface.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start a new session while an existing Dev Container Agent Host is automatically reconnecting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new connect call now waits for the existing remote-host connection to leave connecting/reconnecting state before acquiring it; on success, normal replacement-session setup and send proceed. No new container process is started for this warm path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe remote Agent Host connection status until the existing reconnect completes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One listener per joining request, while the underlying reconnect remains one per active workspace; each status event scans the typically small connection list for the matching address.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: connect returned the cached active target immediately even while its underlying connection was reconnecting; downstream remote work still depended on that host becoming usable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The reconnect completion is intentionally placed on the new-session critical path so setup does not use a reconnecting host.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reuse the existing Dev Container transport rather than launch a second CLI connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero new subprocesses on the active reconnecting path; one existing reconnect per workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same active transport was reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No additional subprocess blocks the join; only connection readiness does.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneous draft submissions targeting the same reconnecting workspace, realistically small because the visible composer owns one draft; each listener performs a linear lookup across registered remote connections.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The transport owns a single reconnect. Joiners wait independently on the same connection-status event stream; they do not initiate parallel container starts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The warm _activeConnections entry prevents cold connection creation. If status becomes disconnected, the wait fails rather than populating a negative cache; later explicit retry follows the existing connection path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the branch, event predicate, active-connection reuse, and tests for connected/canceled/disconnected outcomes are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reconnect duration can be long, but it already gates useful remote work. The added local event/list scan cost is small and bounded by active connections and joiners.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff serializes the join behind an already-required reconnect without increasing remote-operation cardinality or starting duplicate containers.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render transcript preparation progress and connection-log actions in chat/session UI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Observable progress updates synchronously replace one short rendered status message, update a reused Link and context key, and toggle input inert/read-only state only when cancellable preparation begins or ends. Existing-session connection status updates similarly update one reused detail link.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Render a short Markdown progress message and update a bounded set of DOM nodes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per observable progress/status transition. Dev Container preparation emits a constant number of phases; CLI output is not streamed into this renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing transcript progress already recreated the rendered message per update; the diff reuses the progress subpart and adds one persistent detail Link plus bounded input-state toggles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously on the UI update path but is constant-sized and reuses the progress container, progress part, and detail link.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reveal the existing output channel when the user activates Show Log.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One reveal per explicit user activation; channel registration is deduplicated by a normalized-workspace hash.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The output channel already received connection output, but it was not reachable from these progress/recovery surfaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the preparation critical path unless the user explicitly requests it; revealing does not launch or reconnect the container.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant number of preparation phases per draft and one detail DOM node per instantiated chat/recovery surface, not proportional to CLI output, transcript history, or attachment count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI updates are serialized by observables. The preparation view is created once when progress becomes present and disposed when the boolean clears; phase-message changes do not reconstruct it. Repeated log activations are independent user actions but reuse one channel.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The temporary view is lifecycle-scoped to the autorun state, the progress DOM is lazily created once per widget and reused, and output channels are registered once per workspace key.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: observable dependencies, cleanup stores, changed renderer code, and regression tests establish allocation count and disposal behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A full ChatView is heavier than a text node, but only one is visible and retained alongside one preserved composer during a single startup; no evidence shows repeated construction or long-lived accumulation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. New synchronous UI work is constant and lifecycle-bounded, while the implementation avoids per-output-line rendering and repeated view creation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open connection logs for a restored Dev Container provider before its connector is registered
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user-triggered Show Log waits for connector registration (with the existing bounded registration timeout), then reveals a workspace-keyed output channel. Session reconnection itself proceeds independently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for the renderer-side Dev Container connector registration and invoke its output service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded wait per explicit click before registration; after registration, direct channel reveal. No automatic calls are introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no pre-connection log-opening action on restored providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the explicit log-opening action waits; reconnect and session startup are not blocked by it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Explicit user activations and number of restored workspace providers; channel identity is deduplicated per workspace.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No automatic fan-out. Multiple rapid clicks could create multiple timeout-bounded waits, but each requires user action and does not create connections or subprocesses.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The registered connector is reused after initialization, and output-channel registration checks the global channel registry before creating a channel.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: showLog and _waitForConnector call paths are direct and contain no connection creation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Connector registration timing depends on startup, but retained waits are timeout-bounded and not scheduled automatically.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new boundary is user-initiated, bounded, and off session startup’s critical path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 45 changed files and all patch pages. Traced foreground/background draft preparation, optional worktree IPC, Dev Container CLI startup, reconnect joining, temporary chat-view rendering, output-channel reveal, cancellation, and cleanup. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found.
